aiReadyLines.text: 110 ENGLISH FOR TODAY
Write short answers to the following questions: 5x2=10
(a) How did Helen Keller’s father learn about Perkins School for the
Where did Helen Keller begin her formal education?
(c) What was the turning point in Helen Keller's life that affected her
(d) Describe how Anne Sullivan became involved in Helen Keller’s life.
(c} Was Helen Keller’s decision to pursuc education a turning point
in her life? Argue your point.
Read the text and answer the questions 3 & 4
Over time, Shahana grew more devoted to her responsibilitics. She managed her house-
hold duties while excelling in her studies. At school, she gave her best effort in teach-
ing, ensuring that all students, whether struggling or excelling, received her guidance.
Her students frequently sought her advice, not just in the classroom but also outside in
the corridors and even beyond school premises. Before long, Shahana earned a reputa-
tion as an outstanding teacher. Students greeted her warmly, and fellow teachers, includ-
ing the Head Teacher, valued her contributions. Parents and community members recog-
nized her dedication and often approached her with appreciation and respect.
Shahana(a) increasingly dedicated to her responsibilities, (b) house-
hold duties with her studies and excelling as a teacher. She provided (c) to all
her students, both inside and outside the classroom, carning a reputation as an outstand-
ing educator. Her (d) were appreciated by students, colleagues, the Head Teach-
er, and the community, (e) respected and admired her dedication.
Read the passage carefully and replace the following words
with their suitable synonyms or antonyms. 1x5=5
(a} Devote (Antonym)
(b) Struggle (Synonym)
(c) Premises (Synonym)
(d) Corridor (Synonym)
(e) Appreciate (Antonym)

110 ENGLISH FOR TODAY
2. Write short answers to the following questions: 5x2=10
(a) How did Helen Keller’s father learn about Perkins School for the
Where did Helen Keller begin her formal education?
(c) What was the turning point in Helen Keller's life that affected her
(d) Describe how Anne Sullivan became involved in Helen Keller’s life.
(c} Was Helen Keller’s decision to pursuc education a turning point
in her life? Argue your point.
Read the text and answer the questions 3 & 4
Over time, Shahana grew more devoted to her responsibilitics. She managed her house-
hold duties while excelling in her studies. At school, she gave her best effort in teach-
ing, ensuring that all students, whether struggling or excelling, received her guidance.
Her students frequently sought her advice, not just in the classroom but also outside in
the corridors and even beyond school premises. Before long, Shahana earned a reputa-
tion as an outstanding teacher. Students greeted her warmly, and fellow teachers, includ-
ing the Head Teacher, valued her contributions. Parents and community members recog-
nized her dedication and often approached her with appreciation and respect.
3. Complete the passage with suitable words: 1x5=5
Shahana(a) increasingly dedicated to her responsibilities, (b) house-
hold duties with her studies and excelling as a teacher. She provided (c) to all
her students, both inside and outside the classroom, carning a reputation as an outstand-
ing educator. Her (d) were appreciated by students, colleagues, the Head Teach-
er, and the community, (e) respected and admired her dedication.
4. Read the passage carefully and replace the following words
with their suitable synonyms or antonyms. 1x5=5
(a} Devote (Antonym)
(b) Struggle (Synonym)
(c) Premises (Synonym)
(d) Corridor (Synonym)
(e) Appreciate (Antonym)
